question: Which of the following systems of therapeutic prescription seems the most adequate to avoid errors in the treatment of the hospitalized patient?

options.opa: Report directly to the most trusted nurse.
options.opb: Handwriting all the details of the treatment.
options.opc: Dictate the treatment to the secretary so that it passes to the nurse.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Handwriting all the details of the treatment -> increases the risk of errors due to illegibility -> 70% CHAIN: Dictate the treatment to the secretary so that it passes to the nurse -> may introduce transcription errors -> 60% CHAIN: Complete the electronic prescription record -> reduces the risk of errors due to legibility issues -> 85% CHAIN: Report directly to the most trusted nurse -> minimizes the risk of errors by direct communication -> 70%
analysis: The most adequate system to avoid errors in the treatment of the hospitalized patient is to complete the electronic prescription record. Electronic prescriptions help reduce errors related to illegible handwriting, improve communication between healthcare providers, and provide decision support to ensure appropriate dosing and drug interactions.
